We need a new kind of company and a new kind of team to re-accelerate progress. Boom is America's most vertically-integrated aviation and energy company—and we're here to do the important things that the big guys can't or won't do.

We already made history with XB-1, the first privately developed supersonic jet. Next, we're turning our supersonic engine technology into Superpower. Then, it's time for Overture—the supersonic airliner that will carry our friends, family, and loved ones.

Each phase sets up the next. XB-1 proved a small team could build a supersonic jet and break the sound barrier. The engine core we’re designing starts its life on the ground as Superpower, generating power for AI data centers. This then opens the path for us to create our own engine for Overture. Overture then opens the way to a family of supersonic aircraft.
Twice as fast as today's airliners, 50% faster when boomless. More comfortable, safer, and dramatically more affordable than Concorde. Pre-ordered by United, American, and Japan Airlines.
We'll ultimately produce an entire family of supersonic craft of various sizes and ranges, with the goal of making safe, comfortable, affordable supersonic flight available to all passengers.
Head of Executive Projects
Ultimately, fares are up to our airline partners. We’ve designed Overture to be profitable for airlines at fares similar to first and business class across hundreds of transoceanic routes.
Now, we are taking all the learnings from the XB-1 program and scaling them up to deliver supersonic travel with Overture, cutting travel times in half for millions of passengers around the world.

No. The afterburners on Concorde caused loud noise levels at takeoff. Overture will not have afterburners. Overture will be powered by the Symphony propulsion system, and have a landing and takeoff noise output similar to today’s subsonic aircraft. Symphony is a medium bypass ratio turbofan engine, which will be much quieter than Concorde’s turbojet engines with afterburners.

As a passenger aircraft, Overture will go through the same FAA certification process as all other commercial airplanes flying today. This program includes putting the aircraft through lightning strikes, heavy crosswinds, extreme hot and cold temperatures, and simulated emergencies.
Will your aircraft be offered as a private jet?

Our primary mission is to build a commercial passenger aircraft that is profitable for our airline customers to operate. We’re targeting a large unmet market need in transoceanic commercial air travel, which will be accessible to millions of people flying on hundreds of aircraft.

Boom’s supersonic demonstrator aircraft, XB-1, broke the sound barrier six times without creating an audible sonic boom heard on the ground. With the success of the XB-1 flight test program, Boom announced Boomless Cruise for the Overture airliner, which allows for supersonic speeds without an audible sonic boom that reaches the ground.

Leveraging well-known Mach cutoff physics, a sonic boom refracts upward due to temperature and wind gradients affecting the local speed of sound. This is similar to how light bends when passing through a glass of water. By flying at a sufficiently high altitude at an appropriate speed for current atmospheric conditions, Overture’s sonic boom never reaches the ground.
Not a single-process operator
Most technician jobs put you on one machine, running one qualified process, all day. You get very good at one thing, and the interesting decisions get made without you.
Fabricate, build, and finish real parts across many processes - additive (metal, ceramic, polymer), investment casting, heat treatment, and general shop and lab work.
Work directly with Advanced Process engineers to take rough concepts and get hardware in hand fast - then iterate.
Set up and run development trials, capture what happened, and feed results back so the process gets better.

The process you need often won't exist yet - you'll help invent it, and most of what you try won't work the first time. The domains are broad and you'll be learning constantly. The parts you make go into real engines, so your safety discipline, craft, and documentation have to be absolute. If a build looks off, we need to know that more than we need it to look finished.
A track record of teaching yourself new machines and processes.
Comfort in a fast-paced, ambiguous R&D environment where the procedure is still being written - and resilience when things fail.

Unlike "low boom" designs, Boomless Cruise does not require extensive aircraft shaping. It relies on breaking the sound barrier at high altitude where the boom refracts away. Symphony engines enable efficient supersonic transition above 30,000 feet. An advanced autopilot uses weather conditions and software algorithms to automatically select optimal Boomless Cruise speed.

Overture is most efficient at high subsonic speeds of Mach 0.94 and supersonic speed of Mach 1.7. Aerodynamic drag increases closer to the sound barrier, causing a modest fuel burn increase at low supersonic speeds. Despite this, Overture has sufficient range for the longest transcontinental routes like Vancouver–Miami.

San Francisco to New York takes 3 hours 25 minutes instead of just over 5 hours, saving more than 90 minutes. Passengers can leave Washington, DC at 8:00AM EST and arrive in Los Angeles in 3 hours 40 minutes at 8:40AM PST.

「超音速ジェットをもう一度！」Boom Supersonicが挑む空の旅の革命
昔、「コンコルド」という超音速旅客機があったのを覚えているでしょうか？音速の2倍で飛んで、ニューヨークとロンドンを約3時間半で結んでいたんですが、2003年に運航が停止されてしまいました。
今回は、そのコンコルドの後継者として注目されるスタートアップ「Boom Supersonic」の創業者、ブレイク・ショールさんが超音速旅客機を再び空に飛ばすまでの物語をまとめてみました。
ブレイクさんが博物館でコンコルドを見たとき、「なんでこんな素晴らしい飛行機がなくなったんだろう？」という疑問を持ちました。
調べてみると、原因は技術ではなく、料金の高さや運航コストの問題だったことが分かりました。コンコルドのチケットは非常に高額で、しかも空席が目立つような状況でした。
実はブレイクさん、航空業界とは全く無縁の人。Amazonでエンジニアをして、その後スタートアップを立ち上げて売却したテック業界の人間でした。彼が持っていたのは「パイロットの資格」と「超音速飛行への情熱」だけ。
でも彼は「情熱さえあれば、どんなことでも学べる」と信じて、航空工学の本を買い込み、微積分や物理を一から勉強し直しました。
